correctness.rationale: For a generic Haar-random central normal u, every vertex of B(a)∩u^⊥ corresponds bijectively to a transversely intersected box edge. There are 2^(d-1) edges in each direction i. Gaussian representation u=G/||G|| gives the crossing event |Σ_{j!=i}ε_j a_jG_j|<a_i|G_i| for independent centered normals, so its probability is (2/π)arcsin[a_i/(Σa_j²)^(1/2)]. Summing exact indicators establishes E[V]=2^d/π Σ_i arcsin sqrt(p_i). For f(p)=arcsin sqrt p, f'(p)=1/[2sqrt(p(1-p))]; if x>y and x+y<1 then x(1-x)>y(1-y), hence f'(x)<f'(y). Every nontrivial balancing transfer increases the sum whenever d>=3 and all p_i>0; d>=4 in claimed scope. The cube is the unique maximizer; successive coordinate mergers give strict lower infimum 2^(d-1), attained only as a boundary limit. Taylor f''(1/d)=-(d-2)d²/[4(d-1)^(3/2)] gives deficit coefficient (2^d/π)(d-2)d²/[8(d-1)^(3/2)], and the 4-cube expectation is exactly 32/3. Independent 4D Gaussian edge-count Monte Carlo reproduced 10.6667 and asymmetric-case predicted values within sample error; the exact result and strict inequalities are analytic, not Monte Carlo consequences.
